newsitem.title: CHINA: SHENZHEN B INDEX DIPS AT NOON, SEEN TO HOLD.
newsitem.headline: SHENZHEN B INDEX DIPS AT NOON, SEEN TO HOLD.

text.p: Shenzhen's hard currency B shares edged lower in light Tuesday morning trading, but the resumption of trading of shares which just released strong interim results was expected to brighten the mood in the afternoon, brokers said.
The index slipped 0.19 points or 0.14 percent to 132.70 on turnover of HK$26 million.
"The B share index may rebound in the afternoon when stocks which announced strong interim results this morning resume trading," an analyst at J&A Securities (HK) said.

Shenzhen Fiyta Holdings Ltd reported on Tuesday morning a 85 percent year-on-year jump in its 1997 first half net profits, while market giant Shenzhen Fangda Industrial Co Ltd posted a 71 percent first half net rise.
Trading in both issues was suspended in the morning for the announcement.
Shenzhen's B shares dipped in the morning with little rumour or news to fuel buying, analysts said.
"I don't think the index can fall much further as the average P/E ratio has dropped below 11 times," an analyst at China Securities Co Ltd said.
The picture for the yuan-based A share market, which fell 3.46 points or 0.88 percent to 391.73 on light turnover of 1.7 billion yuan, may be different, analysts said.
"The average A share P/E is hovering at about 20 to 25 times, with more room to drop," the China Securities analyst said.
In the B share market, the biggest loser was Shenzhen SEG Co Ltd, which fell 3.39 percent to HK$5.70.
In the A share market, the worst performer was Wuhan Plastics Industrial Group Co Ltd, which plunged to its 10 percent limit-down level of 16.20 yuan.
